findingsAddressed.title: review-S precondition permits a Review when the matching Verdict requires Revision
findingsAddressed.rootCause: The spec 'Change-level Action 前置条件矩阵' requirement description said 'review-explore 需 ...（Current Review=null OR 无 lineage match OR match+changes-requested）'. The 'OR match+changes-requested' clause contradicted the lineage model (match+cr → revise-S) and allowed canRun(review-S) to return allowed:true when a revision was required. Tasks 4.3/4.6/4.9 carried the same error. The conclusion's concrete condition was correct (Current Review=null OR reviewedRunId ≠ Current Artifact Run.runId), but the spec/tasks inherited a contradictory wording.
findingsAddressed.fix: Removed 'OR match+changes-requested' from the spec description and tasks 4.3/4.6/4.9. Added explicit statement that canRun(review-S) MUST return allowed:false on lineage match + changes-requested. Added design decision D1-10 formalizing next↔canRun consistency for review-S. Added 5 new spec scenarios proving: (1) review-S blocks on match+cr; (2) review-propose lineage condition; (3) review-apply lineage condition; (4) unified review blocks on match+cr; (5) unified review restores after revise-S. Added tasks 4.15/9.5/10.20 for table-driven enforcement across all 3 stages.
findingsAddressed.verificationEvidence: Spec description no longer contains 'OR match+changes-requested'. New scenario 'review-S 在 match+changes-requested 时拒绝' explicitly asserts allowed:false + unmetPreconditions:matching-changes-requested-requires-revision. Unified review scenarios prove blocked→restore cycle. openspec validate --strict passed. Full consistencyScan (13 dimensions) verifies cross-reference consistency with 0 contradictions.

keyFindings: D1-PR-002 is a content defect: the spec description and tasks erroneously allowed review-S on match+changes-requested, conflicting with the lineage model.
The conclusion's concrete condition was already correct; the contradiction was introduced when translating to spec/tasks.
D1-10 formalizes that next and canRun MUST apply the same review-S allowance rule: both allow review-S only on no-current-review or no-lineage-match.
Unified review delegates to canRun(review-S), so it now correctly blocks on match+cr and restores only after revise-S produces a new artifact (no match).
5 new spec scenarios + 3 new tasks enforce the fix with table-driven coverage across all 3 stages.
